sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Sweeney is the anglicized form of Suibhne, the mad king of Irish legend. Monaghan sends the reader from Sweeney to the full entry under SUIBHNE. In that account Suibhne was a king of a small region of Ulster. He insulted a saint and a curse fell on him. At the height of a battle he lost his wits and believed he was a bird. He climbed a yew tree and moved from tree to tree across the land. He spoke at last with Saint Molling and told his adventures. Then a man stabbed him with a spear and he died. Some scholars read Suibhne as an Irish form of the wild seer Merlin. For the complete story, see the entry SUIBHNE.
